The Thesis Check: Confirmed, Extended, or Contradicted

The July initiation rested on three legs: the strongest business quality score this framework has issued (8.81, Elite, July 2026 re-score), the cheapest price per unit of quality in the cohort, and a do-not-adopt stance on the rumored round paired with the read that the talks themselves were a forward signal of demand. The term sheet confirms the third leg and extends it: the signal did not merely survive, it firmed at a price above the talked range, with a named lead and a company announcement in place of sourced whispers.

The quality-adjusted price survives the higher bid. At the completed mark the market pays $15.2 billion per point of business quality; at the announced mark it would pay roughly $21.3 billion per point (est., derived). Both numbers sit on the cohort floor by a wide margin: the nearest neighbor pays about $118 billion per point and the top of the ladder sits near $188 billion per point on marks confirmed in mid-July (internal framework on PitchBook-confirmed marks, July 2026; derived). Even granting the full re-rate, the buyer at $188 billion still pays roughly a fifth of the cohort's next-cheapest price per unit of quality. Figure 3 restates the ladder at both marks.

Growth adjustment tells the same story. At 27.2x on $6.9 billion growing +80%, the announced mark prices each point of growth at 0.34x; the listed comparable trades near 15.3x its guided forward product revenue growing +31%, or 0.49x per point (comparable company 8-K, May 27, 2026; derived). The February conclusion, that Databricks is the cheaper growth-adjusted asset, holds at the higher bid. Capital efficiency is the one line that moves against the thesis on close: funds received would lift lifetime equity from roughly $20.2 billion toward $23.2 billion, diluting CE from 0.34x toward 0.30x unless the September print raises the numerator first (derived, equity-only basis). That is a measurement note, not a crack: a company choosing dilution at 40% above its last mark, in a round it does not need, is exercising exactly the capital character the CE dimension scores.

Trigger review: the round trigger from the initiation fired on July 17, and it fired in the direction the report did not predict, firming at a higher price rather than closing or lapsing at the talked range. The margin-gate trigger remains armed and is unchanged by any of this: 74% against the 70% floor, a four-point cushion, guided lower, with the September to October print as the test. The S-1 trigger remains armed with nothing on file at the last registry check. A new trigger is armed today: the close itself, expected before the end of summer, which on completion adopts $188 billion as the mark and re-runs the appraisal.
